articleTitle: The effect of local bone density on stability of dental implants: a finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Finding the ideal replacement for lost teeth has been a key area of interest in restorative dentistry. Despite the advances in dental implantology, failure of the dental implant are still frequent. The relationship between local bone properties and the implant design is arguably have an impact on the implant stability. This study aimed at computationally assessing the suitability of implant materials for various locations in the maxilla and mandible taking into account the variation in cortical and cancellous bone densities. In particular, we examined Titanium and Zirconia as two potential materials for anterior (incisor) and posterior (molar) implants in the maxilla and mandible utilizing finite element analysis. A geometrical model representing the implant and the paraimplant bone was developed. Different bone locations were defined by varying bone material parameters based on the local bone densities. Stress induced in the implant and the cancellous bone were examined under 114. 6N compressive load. The highest stress in the cancellous bone was predicted when Titanium implant was used at the maxilla incisor location (4.01 MPa). Unlike Titanium implant, no change in predicted stress at the four locations was observed when Zirconia implant was used. In general, Zirconia implant resulted in a slightly higher stress in the cancellous bone compared to Titanium implant with one exception; at the incisor location of the maxilla where Titanium induced a slightly higher stress. The study showed that different implant materials can induce distinct mechanical stresses in the cancellous bone. Such impact motivates the need to carefully assess the properties of local cancellous bone when selecting the implant material.

articleTitle: Prediction of Landfill Gas Emissions and Energy Recovery Potential from an Engineered Landfill, in Khartoum State-Sudan
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Organic matter decomposition in landfill produce landfill gas with a major content of methane (CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>), the paper's aim was to estimate the amount of CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> emitted from a landfill cell located at Khartoum Sudan. Landfill gas emissions model was used to predict total landfill gas. The prediction period was set to 50 years, and it was found that the LFG emitted from the cell varies from 10.3 m3/year to 27.6 m3/ year; one year after cell closure the LFG will reach its peak value of 27.6m3/year. In case of energy recovery, the energy potential was 317.3 MJ in 2018 and this year representing the peak year thus the energy recovery start to fall down years later; and would be 265.1 MJ in 2027. While the value of electrical power was found 26.4 kWh in 2018, and by 2027 the plant would produce about 22.1 kWh. Thus producing power from landfill cell would help to reduce the greenhouse gas emission from landfill sites and also reduce the using of fossil fuels which result in decreasing of global warming contribution; the produced power could be fed to national grid.

articleTitle: Tracking Control of Pneumatic Muscle Using Adaptive Passivity Based Control
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Quantitative understanding of the mathematical model of pneumatic muscle (PM) is technically indispensable in control arrangement design for effective real-time execution. In this paper, a robust adaptive tracking method using passivity based control (PBC) techniques is developed and applied to a pneumatic muscle actuator (PMA) pulling a mass against gravity. Pneumatic actuators offer high performance at low cost, but their effective use is often hindered by external disturbances as a direct result of operating conditions. To enhance control performance and robustness for accurate trajectory tracking, we adopted a control objective to force the PM to track specified reference path in the presence of disturbances. A simulation is presented to analyse the behaviour of the proposed scheme. The simulation results verified that the model and the Adaptive Passivity Based Control (APBC) controller achieved required performance in tracking a demand trajectory within the particular accuracy.

articleTitle: Computational investigation of the effect of loading conditions on traumatic mandibular fracture
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: The mandible is the most common site of craniofacial fractures due to trauma. In forensic analysis, it is important to have tools that help investigating the amount, direction and location of impact force the causes of mandibular fractures. Finite element analysis can provide a powerful tool in such investigations. Finite element models were developed to computationally investigate the relationship between the direction/location of impact load and the potential location of the mandibular fracture. A 2000N impact force was applied on four different patterns on the mandible surface: lateral, bilateral, axial and transverse. The maximum stresses and strain, which indicate the location fractures, were found to occur either on the condyles or on the site of force application due to induced bending moment. Condyles were found to be the most vulnerable sites irrespective of the force direction. Our models suggested that symphysis fractures were associated with a direct transverse impact to this site or with a bilateral loads on the body. It was also suggested that body and ramus fractures were either associated with a direct impact force to these regions or due to impact load at the symphysis. This study demonstrated the usefulness of finite element analysis in the investigation of the relationship between the direction of impact force and mandibular fracture locations which could be utilized in post-trauma forensic analysis.

articleTitle: On the Optimization of Spherical Convolution Integral: Efficiency Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: We test the performance of an optimized algorithm that reduces the total run time (TRT) of the numerical evaluation of the spherical convolution integrals for geoid computation. For practical considerations, the performance of the algorithm is tested based on the Stokes's convolution which is used for the determination of regional geoid modeling from the terrestrial gravity measurements. The optimization algorithm is presented in Matlab Software to accelerate the computation's run time using vectorization techniques and relational operators. The presented algorithm is validated over different gravity grid resolutions and spherical capsize values σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> over the selected area. The optimized algorithm shows merits in all testing parameters in both kernel performance and TRT. The TRT of the geoid determination yields 7 times improvements over the largest σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and most dense resolution grid (1 × 1 arc-min) where large data are truncated. A numerical investigation is conducted thoroughly over all suggested scenarios and shows high efficiency. The Matlab vectorization techniques and the relational operators are found to be very efficient to improve the code performance.

articleTitle: Ultrasound strain elastographic based automatic quantitative analysis for evaluation of solid breast lesion
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study to demonstrate the role of ultrasound elastographic imaging for the diagnosis of solid breast lesions. The present work was performed using static deformation on a mimic ultrasound phantom. Strain image is constructed from the measured RF ultrasound signal. The mean strain is recovered from stiffer segmented lesion and from nearby normal tissue, and then compute strain ratio. The stiffness measurement was used to know whether there are already abnormalities in the breast tissue or not. The strain ratio value is a highly significant quantitative method for evaluating the stiffness degree of the breast mass. The experimental result shows that the strain ratio has low value (0. 4) suggesting a malignant lesion.

articleTitle: Application of Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting with an Industrial Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting (PEH) system was implemented with Parallel Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor (P-SSHI) interface with an industrial machine, the Combi-Cleaner from Bühler AG©used in flour production. The implemented system used the PEH system to recharge a drained Nickel Metal Hydride (NiMH) battery to assess the technology's potential of becoming a large-scale clean power supplement. The device was implemented in three different positions on the machine and generated a total of 0.24V in 30 minutes of operation. This is a promising output since these machines work endlessly and highlights future areas of research specific to the application of PEH in the industrial field.

articleTitle: Detection of CT-Liver Lesions using Otsu Algorithm and Morphological Operations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: The incidence of liver lesions has increaseddramatically in recent years. Early diagnosis is the best solution for rescuing patients exposed to this type of cancer. The aims of this study are to diagnosis early stages of liver lesions to increase the information for proper diagnose, by designing an effective and accurse method to detect the lesions which uses to enhance the CT images resolution and reduce the noise that may affect computed tomography (CT)-abdomen images and calculate values of intensities of anatomical structures of the liver in the so called histogram to determine the extent of intensities of the infected and non-infected regions also design simple method to compute histogram and probabilities of each intensity level to separate regions using the set threshold which applied for all pixels of the image to segment the lesions regions. The methodology was included the use of Digital Image Processing techniques, First CT-abdomen images database were acquired from local hospital and registered image from online atlas database, the noises were removed using smoothing and sharpening filters. These filters were estimated to select best performance filters, Evaluation were implemented using two common parameters mean square error (MSE) and signal to noise ratio (SNR), the evaluation conducted [5*5], [7*7],[9*9] for both smoothing and sharpening filter. Sharpen filter with size [9*9] showed better results in both parameters. Secondly, the histogram was calculated which represent the intensities of each elements in the image. After that the mathematical modeling of Otsu method which was used to calculate threshold values for affected regions detection. After lesions segmentation stage, morphological operations were used to enhance the lesions boundaries. The obtain results evaluate the criterion for maximizing the between class variance to extract the segmented lesions with goodness factor called entropy parameter, which compute the randomness in an image and it gave values between (0.6739-0.9706) which indicated the effectiveness of the method in detecting liver lesions.

articleTitle: CFD Modelling of The Turbulent Flow in Mathematical Models of The Human Central Airways
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: The airflow in human airways is numerically investigated in a symmetrical three-dimensional airway bifurcation model using Computational Fluid Dynamic (CFD). Numerical simulations are carried out for two different geometrical models. Based on Weibel's model of human airways, the first model consists of the trachea (generation 0) and the first daughter generation branches. To develop the second model, the geometry of the first model is extended to the second-generation daughter branches. Simulations were carried out for three different inlet velocities utilizing both the standard k-ε-model and Large Eddy Simulation (LES) model. The aim of the study is to evaluate the use of the LES model and the standard k-ε-model for modelling the airflow in the human airways. The results show that the standard k-ε-model better predict the bronchial flow in comparison to published experimental data. Moreover, Asthma drug delivery is also investigated. Particles of 9 μm diameters, reflecting the size of common asthma-treatment drugs, are induced at an inlet velocity of 3.03 m/s and a mass flow rate of 200 mg/s.

articleTitle: Irradiance Variation Effect on the Electrical Performance of a Grid Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Electrical power is generated when exposing photovoltaic cells (PV) to direct sun light. The sun irradiance causes the movement of the electrons that generate the electric current. According to PV cells' characteristics the amount of sun irradiance effects on the generated electric energy. This paper studies and investigates the effect of exposing different irradiance values to a grid connected PV system of 250 kW connected to a 33kV grid via a three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI). The PV system has been designed and simulated by MATLAB/Simulink environment. Sun irradiance does not remain constant all over the day, this effects on the performance of the PV system. Atmospheric conditions also effect on the amount of solar irradiance. Different investigations have been done by studying the electrical performance of the system at various irradiance values. This study had proved that the increase of the irradiance amount increases the generated electrical power till reaching the saturation point of the PV cell, then no more increment occurs on the generated power.

articleTitle: Local Search Heuristic for the Optimisation of Flight Connections
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Kiwi.com proposed a real-world NP-hard optimisation problem with a focus on air travelling services, determining the cheapest connection between specific areas. Despite some similarities with the classical TSP problem, more complexity is involved that makes the problem unique. It is Time-dependent, Asymmetric and involves areas that contain sets of cities from which exactly one is visited. In addition to this, infeasibility adds more complexity to the problem since there are no flights available between specific points in the network for certain days. While solving such computationally difficult problems, exact methods often fail, particularly when the problem instance size increases; Then alternative approaches, such as heuristics, are preferred in problem solving. In this study, we present an effective local search method for solving Kiwi.com problem. The empirical results show the success of the approach, which embeds four simple operators, on most of the released instances.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Simplified Wireless Area Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSN) systems face many delivery and reliability problems. In this paper we implement a relaying and routing scheme in order to solve these problems. The maximum coverage area for a single node is tested, and to extend the coverage are an additional node is added. A five node WSN system has been implement to assure frame delivery in the event of node failures. The results show that the maximum coverage area for a single node is 33m, for larger distances extra nodes need to be added. Results also showed that a reliably delivery can be achieved by implementing multiple path between the source and destination.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of High Power Stripline Directional coupler For VHF Radars
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This paper presents design and implementation of stripline directional coupler to be used for power monitoring (direct and reflected) in VHF radar transmitters. The coupler is designed between 130 MHZ to 180 MHZ and with a coupling of 38.6+0.3 dB and also to be low loss, good matched and with a directivity that is better than 20 dB. The coupler is designed and simulated with the help of ADS program, then it is fabricated and measured using Vector network analyzer (VNA). Simulation and measurements results are compared. The measurements results which are represented in terms of scattering parameters shows that, the proposed coupler has a coupling of 37.8 dB to 38.1 dB with a directivity that is better than 23 dB.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Basal Metabolic Rate Heating Effect in Hepatic Microwave Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia is one of the promising techniques for hepatic cancer treatment. Studying heat transfer parameters in biological tissues plays main role in understanding treatment process. In this paper, a study of Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) effect in microwave hyperthermia for hepatic tumors was introduced. A floating sleeve antenna was designed and used as a heat source with a 3D liver model to study the effect of changing the BMR in temperature elevation. This was implemented using modelling and simulation in Computer Simulation Technology (CST) platform. Different values were assigned to BMR and the temperature distribution was registered each time. The obtained results showed that the temperature increased by about 0.4 °C each time the BMR increased. In addition, when the BMR is 11 times the surroundings liver tissues and more, a good temperature distribution was observed. The study concluded that the hepatic tumor could be damage by microwave hyperthermia considering that the tumor BMR is 11-20 times the liver tissues.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of In-network Caching Strategies for Information Centric Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: One of the most efficient methods to decrease the overall network traffic is through the deployment of distributed caching systems. Thus, are many proposed strategies to determine where to locate the caches within a network to maximize its performance. However, among all these strategies, it is still unclear, which one performs better. In this paper, the in-network caching strategies for Information Centric Networks (ICN) are studied. A neutral simulation framework is used to measure the performance in terms of cache hit ratio, content delivery latency, and the generated link load. The study considers different cache positioning strategies i.e., Leave Copy Everywhere (LCE), Leave Copy Down (LCD) and Probabilistic Caching (Probcache), different content popularities range, a variety of cache sizes and a couple of eviction policies i.e., Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Frequently Used (LFU) algorithms. Results show that when LRU implemented as an eviction policy, the ProbCache performs better than LCD by average of 3% on the cache hit ratio when the cache size is small i.e., (.002,.004) with height content popularity value i.e., (.8, 1, 1.2) and better than LCE by average of 27% where LCD performs better in bigger cache size i.e., (.01,.05). Furthermore, we concluded with that, if we implement LFU as an eviction policy, the LCE and LCD strategies are the best strategy that fit's the environment regarding the cache hit ratio and latency. Additionally, it is noticeable when LFU is implemented the cache hit ratio increases by average of 20% from LRU.

articleTitle: Proposed Model for Arabic Grammar Error Correction Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Deep learning and machine learning algorithms are widely used in Arabic Natural Language Processing (ANLP) aims to develop tools and techniques to process human languages in several forms like written and spoken context. The ANLP still lacks tools and applications to bridge the hole between Arabic and other languages. Furthermore, there are insufficient available resources such as dictionaries, grammatical rules, corpora, etc. Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) one of the NLP tasks seek to develop automatic tools to correct grammar and spelling, the input is incorrect words or sentences and the output become the corrected version of the same sentences. Recently, Neural Networks are used in GEC and had promising results but some improvement is still needed. The limitation of the previous studies are handcrafted and most often extracted from short sentences, also the whole previous Arabic neural approaches are used Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). This paper present work-in-progress for developing an Arabic GEC model based on multi convolutional layers with an attention mechanism. Moreover, proposed the incremental techniques and multi-round training model using parallel corpus to get more accuracy and fluently results, also to achieve human-level performance.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network for a Self-Driving Car in a Virtual Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are machine learning models accomplishing state of the art results in a variety of computer vision tasks, decision making and visual recognition. For a long time, traditional computer vision based algorithms has been the primary method for analyzing camera footage, used for assisting safety functions, where decision making have been a product of manually constructed behaviors. During the last few years deep learning has showed its extraordinary capabilities for both visual recognition and decision making in end-to-end systems. this paper proposes a solution of introducing redundancy by combining deep learning methods with traditional computer vision based techniques for minimizing unsafe behavior in autonomous vehicles. A CNN has been trained to map raw pixels from a single front-facing camera directly to steering commands. The objective was to build a simple and reliable algorithm for a self-driving car and to implement a system that allow autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Waste to Energy as an Alternative Energy Source and Waste Management Solution
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Recently, one of the major and serious worldly concerns is the limitation of energy resources. Developing countries in specific, confronts a critical crises relating to fossil fuel resources, and mostly concerning the production of electricity energy from fired thermal power plants. The urbanization and economic growth, have significantly contributed to the municipal solid waste (MSW) generation increase. The massive volume of the generated waste in developing countries requires sustainable management. MSW high generation rate make it difficult to handle in a proper way. As the energy demand has increased during past years due to the massive consumption rate, in the context of meet the future energy demand with low health issues and environment crisis; a new technologies must introduced. Therefore, this paper presents a review on WTE technology as a solution of MSW problem and providing alternative source of energy. WTE technologies mean utilizing waste to generate energy or converting garbage to be alternative energy source. Biological treatment is showing in the biogas utilization; landfill sites could also produce LFG with massive amount which have the ability to produce power as it have 30% CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> content by volume in the total stream, The Reppie thermal plant is considered a solution for both waste and energy sectors as it produce power to cover 30% of city households electricity needs. Increasing the level of awareness to environmental practices would help to present and support WTE technologies, as people behavior towards waste could help to establish a proper waste management hierarchy that activate reduce, reuse and recycling programs before goes to disposal or burin stage.

articleTitle: Design of Speed Control System of DC motor Based on PID tuning with fuzzy define weighting point
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: considering the non-linear characteristics of the DC motors and the design challenges under the mechanical changes due to the ambient conditions. Moreover, precise control cannot be achieved using only classical PID control. This paper proposes a novel technique for optimizing the speed of the separately excited DC motor. This optimization process is accomplished by decreasing the rise time, settling time and overshoot characteristics. Fuzzy logic in cooperation with PID is used to implement an appropriate performance. As well known the conventional fuzzy has no integral part, and the weak point of the PID is the overshoot. This paper combines both the fuzzy logic and PID control using a weighting point in proportional action to achieve an enhanced controller. Moreover, acquire the advantages of both methods. Consequently, a balancing is attained between the overshoot and the rise time in the motor speed response. Matlab Simulink is used to model the DC motor then fuzzy define weighting point method applied to control the motor speed. The comprehensive simulation results show that the design has a faster response, no overshoot, better robustness, and dynamic and static performance. It outperforms the classical control techniques for attaining high precise control.

Author Keywords: Membership Functions(MF). fuzzy define weighting point (FDWP)

articleTitle: A Comparison between Different Classifiers for Diagnoses of Atrial Fibrillation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This study is a comparison study with the purpose to propose an approach for selecting the best classifier for diagnoses of atrial fibrillation (AF) in coronary heartbeats. The Physionet Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2017 turned into used as the data source for this study. Automatic ECG processing consists essentially of the detection and location of the signal characteristic points and is an important tool in the management of cardiac diseases. The most relevant task is the detection of the QRS complex after which a complete analysis and delineation of each beat can be obtained. In the preprocessing stage, the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is used for removing noise and tuning to the morphological characteristics of the waveform features. For feature extraction, a set of features that consists of both morphological and temporal features is extracted using DWT. A comparison study was conducted between five classifiers (Decision trees, Random forest, AdaBoost ensemble classifier, support vector machine (SVM) and K-nearest neighbor Algorithm (KNN)) to know which give the best diagnoses for each type of Arrhythmia. In this study we used four classes of coronary heart beats atrial fibrillation, normal, other rhythms or noise. Results show that the AdaBoost classifier gives 100 % Accuracy scores for all types of Arrhythmia in the training set. The AdaBoost algorithm obtained a mean improvement report for all classes in testing set (97.3% in Area under curve accuracy (AUC), 94.7% in classifier accuracy (CA), 96.7% in sensitivity (Recall), and of 98 % in positive predictive value (Precision)).

articleTitle: A Survey on Automatic Fake News Identification Techniques for Online and Socially Produced Data
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Fake news are spread on online sites and social media at an alarming speed and in large quantities. Fake news aim to mislead and deceive readers with verifiable false information and they are published on untrusted websites and social media accounts. As they have a very big impact on readers, it is critical to develop efficient models for detecting fake news. This paper reviews the literature on fake news detection and categorizes detection approaches into Knowledge Based approaches and Machine Learning based approaches. Machine Learning based approaches that have been covered in this paper are divided into Conventional approaches and Neural Network approaches. It provides Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Naïve Bayes for Conventional approaches. In addition to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for Neural Network approaches. Also, the paper discusses the provided approaches.

articleTitle: Application of coyote optimizer for Optimal DG Placement in Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid analytical and metaheuristic optimization technique to find the optimal placement of the distributed generation (DG) in radial distribution system (RDS) considering annual load growth. The main objective of the placement of the DG is to minimize the power losses and improve the voltage profile with considering operation constraints. An efficient meta-heuristic technique known as coyote optimization algorithm (COA) assign the DG locations while the analytical technique calculates the size of the DGs mathematically. The obtained results are very accurate with low computational time. The proposed hybrid method is tested on IEEE 69-bus system and compared with other well-known optimization techniques. Also the obtained results prove the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: power loss reduction & voltage profile improvement

articleTitle: Integration of Downdraft Gasifier with Fuel Cell and Organic Rankine Cycle for Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a combined cycle for producing power in microscale. This cycle consists of three technologies of Biomass gasification (downdraft reactor using air as a reactor agent feeding with oil palm fronds as biomass fuel), solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC), and organic Rankine cycle (ORC) (using Isopentane and R245fa as working fluids). The resulting exhaust of SOFC is used in the ORC. The thermo-dynamic system is simulated using Cycle-Tempo software program. Some parameters such as current density, fuel utilization, pressure ratio, temperature ratio, are taken into account to study their actions on the performance of the overall cycle. After recovering the waste heat from SOFC through ORC under the terms of the design parameter, the summary of results proved that the efficiency is increased by 40%.

articleTitle: A comparative study on human loco-motor activity recognition using wearable sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: In a worldwide scale, the population that suffers from muscular impairments, spinal cord injuries, or lower-limb amputations is estimated to be in millions, this population is in need for advanced rehabilitation devices to help them restore their lower-limb functionality. Accurate recognition of loco-motor activity is of great importance for improving rehabilitation devices that activate and take the correct action according to the current activity. However, this field of activity recognition lacks a comprehensive study on the suitability of some methods, algorithms or sensors over the others. In this paper, we carried out several experiments to reach for the best possible machine learning tools and sensor combinations or placements that can maximize off-line accuracy and minimize prediction time. Starting from a data set that combines sEMG and mechanical sensors placed bilaterally, after we specified 8 different loco-motor activities and extracted features that were used extensively in the literature, we found that EMG signals do not offer a significant improvement in accuracy unlike mechanical sensors which achieved alone an average of 97% accuracy in subject-dependent context. The optimal set of features for mechanical sensors and sEMG sensors were found to be time domain features and wavelet coefficients features respectively. The performance of KNN, LDA, QDA, LR, ANN, ETC and SVM models were compared; at which ETC was found to achieve the highest performance in terms of accuracy 92% and 97% in subject-dependent and subject-independent context respectively. LDA, LR and QDA outperformed the others in terms of time and model size measures.

articleTitle: E-payment Adoption by Petroleum Companies in Sudan
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Despite the increased use of e-payment methods around the world, there is a weak evidence of a switch away from cash usage, especially in Sudan where the demand for cash has risen since the start of the great liquidity crises. Petroleum companies are cash rich because of the massive daily flow of cash at them, although e-payment makes the management of money and the fueling process faster and more convenient, only few petroleum companies adopted these payment methods. To the date of this study no previous studies examine the factors affecting e-payment adoption in Sudan's petroleum companies, which creates a knowledge gap. This study is therefore aimed at filling this gap by seeking to investigate the factors affecting E-payment adoption by the petroleum companies in Sudan. The research adopts Technology, Organization, Environment framework (TOE) to determine the factors influencing the adoption of e-payment from the service provider side. A set of potentially determinant factors of the adoption was organized in three major groups: Technological, Organizational, and Environmental. Data gathered based on convince sampling from Eighteen petroleum companies headquarters in Khartoum State. Employees of different roles were asked to fill a questionnaire in each company. Data analyzed using R statistical environment. After applying different tests on the nine factors, the result indicated that only four of these factors, Compatibility, Security Concerns, Top Management Support, and firm Size are found to be important determinants of the adoption of e-payment and that they have a significant effect on the e-payment choice. The findings of this study could be used by petroleum companies in Sudan to determine what factors the company should optimize in order to adopt e-payment method. The study recommends further researches to focus on identifying and analyzing the factors from consumer's side also to provide a comprehensive study.

articleTitle: X-ray Tube Arc Preventation by Stabilization of Voltage in a Dual Energy CT Scanner: A Review Study
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: For a dual energy CT scanner, rapid switching between two voltage levels is essential for obtaining critical diagnosis information. In order to obtain the best quality diagnosis images, X-ray tubes are operated at maximum power. Under such demand, X-ray tubes are expected to arc. Arc may indicates the end of life expectancy for the tube. Arcing is prone to occur when input potential is increased rapidly. This paper include the improvement of an arc suppressor that has been already patented by Furbee and others. An arc suppressor includes two parallel quadrant assemblies at which one quadrant includes an inductive coil used to store excessive energy during arc event, and later the same energy is dissipated using a high voltage diode. Another method was used which included stabilizing voltage during the full operation of the tube by implementing a PI controller to regulate the voltage and to provide a steady output signal. The system’s capability was tested under three voltage conditions, ranging from normal to high transient potential. Arc suppression and voltage stabilization were very efficient when operating at high kV level rating up to almost 99.9S%. However, the efficiency was slightly decreased to 99.95%, during normal operation and the system might experience a small voltage-overshoot during excessive transient voltages The X-ray tube voltage regulator was simulated and tested using MATLAB Simulink software.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Knapsack Problem for Resource Allocation in a Distributed Competitive Environment Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Internet of Things devices, Smart phones and smart cities have been expanding at wide rates which are highly computation resources demand. Classic cloud computing architecture, cannot continue provide the services requirements exploit by IoT services because of network latency, scalability, and network stability. Edge cloud computing had been introduced as a distributed edge cloud paradigm which provides an opportunity for users to obtain cloud resources over the internet. Services providers deploy the services in a distributed manner among the edge servers. However, the challenge is how to allocate the resources for users from different and distributed edge server. An intelligent strategy would provide a proper resource allocation on edge cloud architecture need to be addressed. In this paper, we consider edge computing architecture as an environment in which edge servers willing to invest their available resources and end-users want to utilize the services according to pay-asyou-go paradigm. Since edge servers need to maximize their profit by serving the maximum number of users. This paper present work-in-progress to overcome this challenge by formulating the problem as multi-dimensional knapsack, then genetic algorithm will proposed to get state of the art results and achieve our goal.

articleTitle: Design of Optimum Nano Scale CMOS Inverter Integrated With RRAM
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This work is concentrated on study of parameters which affect CMOS inverter switching speed. The switching speed is studied depending on the transient parameters which are the rise time and the fall time of an output pulse of the inverter. The transient parameters change according to design parameters of inverter like load capacitance, and channel width per length ratio. Three different studies have been performed to analyze the transient parameters of CMOS inverter. The output voltage fall time for a CMOS inverter is explored in first study. The design of CMOS inverter having symmetrical output voltage with equal rise time and fall time is described in second study. A CMOS inverter with improved symmetrical output voltage with equal rise time and fall time and equal delays when switching from high to low and when switching from low to high is explored in third study. A vision of a hybrid device based on integrating CMOS inverter and RRAM is developed to put a step in the way of merging logic unit and non-volatile memory.

articleTitle: Analysis of Environmental Impact of Gaseous Pathway Released from Hypothetical NPP Site in Sudan
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This study aims to assess the radiation environmental impact of transport and dispersion of airborne radioactive material under the conditions of normal operation of a hypothetical Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) in Sudan, using two types of reactor unit (HL1000 and CNP650 PWR unit) in order to choose the suitable unit type, also the annual effective doses to public have been assessed for both reactor types. In order to achieve these assessments two atmospheric dispersion models have been applied (ROULEA-2.0 and XOQDOQ). The input of these models where metrological data for one year from the geographical site north Port Sudan, source terms and physical parameters from the point of release. The results showed that both types of reactors have no significant environmental impact under normal operating conditions and using two units of CNP650 will have less effect. The annual effective dose for various age group was significantly below the ICRP dose limit. The future work would be to study the environmental impact of liquid pathway release of the NPP as well as the accident conditions.

articleTitle: Online Handwriting Recognition Using Encoder-Decoder Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: In this paper we propose a system that is capable of recognizing raw online handwritten data. The system consists of an advanced type of neural network known as LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) Encoder-decoder combined with a customized attention mechanism layer. The attention mechanism has greatly enhanced the system performance from a low character level accuracy of 53% to an excellent accuracy of 96%. Moreover, the system involves a segmentation algorithm designed to divide the sentences into segments of lines. For the training and testing we employ the IAM On-Line Handwriting database, the source can be found here [1]. The accuracy can be improved even further by integrating our system with a language model to spell check the outputs.

articleTitle: Developed Resonant PIRSMC Control for DFIGWPG System under Harmonic Deformation on the Grid Voltage
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This study offers control strategy for the rotor current in regard to stator-port power signals under sliding mode strategy like proportional and integral control based on the proportional and integral with resonant function as switching surface rule (PIRSMC) for the distorted DFIG-WPGS with varied attitudes and various control aims. The fundamental parts and 5th-/7th-order harmonics at the positive synchronous reference plane of the rotor-port current, vibrations of electromagnetic torque and stator-port power, are adjusted by the offered control with a resonant function harmonic parts adapted at six-times the main grid frequency. Thus, these quantities are instantly adjusted by the PIRSMC technique without additional succession evaluations of the components. The simulation results are implemented using Matlab Simulink for the introduced control of a 2MW DFIGWPGS and have been compared with PISMC and PI control principle.

articleTitle: Improved DFIG-WPGS Efficiency via the tuned PI-Resonant Unit Controller based on BAT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: This study introduces rotor-edge current control concerning stator-edge power behavior based on the online tuned Resonant Proportional-Integral Regulator using Discrete-BAT optimization Algorithm (DPIR-ON-DBAT) for the DFIG-WPGS as a Recurrent Artificial Neural Network (RANN). The DPIR-ON-DBAT is designed to control the distorted system with several dynamic positions and control goals. The +dq rotor-edge current components, swings of electromagnetic torque and stator-edge power, are regulated by the proposed control with a resonant part oscillated at 6-times the main system frequency. Consequently, these variables are instantly regulated by the DPIR-ON-DBAT technique without extra succession disassembling the segments. The simulation results are implemented using Matlab-Simulink for the introduced control of a 2MW DFIG-WPGS, which gave a better dynamic behavior than the customary PIR-Naslin and PI control principle.

articleTitle: Harmonized Software Quality Improvement Models for Sudanese SME Based on CMMI
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Computer, Control, Electrical, and Electronics Engineering (ICCCEEE)
abstract: Software institutions recently implement more than one software process model in order to achieve a high value in their products and services. The challenges of implementing several quality models are increasing the risk of Multi-Model Environment (MME) failure and more resources are needed to support the MME. This kind of resources is not available in the Small and Medium Enterprises (SME), especially in Sudanese institutions. This study aims to provide a solution by encouraging the Sudanese SMEs to apply software models in their software development processes. We are seeking to make these institutions understand how to integrate product quality models with software process improvement models. To achieve this goal, we used a systematic harmonization technique to harmonize and map ISO/IEC 25010 standard onto Capability Maturity Model Integrity (CMMI) Dev 1.3 level 2 and 3. Also, we reviewed the related works of the previous studies on MMEs to achieve better results. The results show some of the processes and activities of CMMI Dev 1.3 considering software quality attributes on the early stage of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). On the other hand, we presented how to apply the mapped models and suggest a tool for implementation. This kind of approach gives small organizations the ability to apply multi SPI models.
